Agreement as a Reference-Free Signal of NL$\\rightarrow$FOL Faithfulness, and Where It Fails}\n\\author{\\vspace{-1cm}}\n\\date{\\vspace{-1cm}}\n\n\\begin{document}\n\\maketitle\n\n\\begin{abstract}\nEvaluating translations of natural language into first-order logic (FOL) without a gold formula is hard: correct formulas are not unique, benchmark gold is often wrong, and LLM judges reward conventional vocabulary. We ask whether agreement among several systems' formalizations of the same sentence, checked by an SMT solver under a vocabulary alignment that never reads predicate names, measures faithfulness to the text. We freeze a peer agreement score weighted by system reliability on 700 development sentences and evaluate it on 450 fresh sentences from MALLS, FOLIO and ProverQA, formalized by nine current LLMs and labelled twice: by a blinded LLM panel and by solver equivalence to audited gold. Peer agreement reaches 0.827 AUROC on panel labels and 0.874 on solver labels, against 0.791 and 0.727 for a gemini-2.5-flash judge. It is invariant to predicate renaming and flags wrong benchmark gold. The evidence for a practical gain is preliminary. Added to a baseline of judge, roundtrip and structural scores, the score gains about 0.03 AUROC on panel labels with an interval that touches zero, and it does not beat an existing Dawid--Skene agreement estimator. It falls below chance on sentences where most systems share an error, which leaves it far behind the judge on long legal definitions. Directional entailment features and error typing added nothing, and two alternatives based on formal structure, a monotonicity signature and judgment worlds built by a solver, did not beat the judge on current systems. Agreement across systems is a complement, invariant to vocabulary, to a judge that reads the text on short sentences, not a replacement for one.\n\\end{abstract}\n\n%======================================================================\n\\section{Introduction}\n\\label{sec:intro}\n\nLarge language models (LLMs) are now the usual semantic parser in pipelines that translate natural-language (NL) text into first-order logic (FOL) and hand the result to a theorem prover or SMT solver \\citep{Pan2023,Olausson2023}. Whether such a pipeline reasons correctly depends first on whether each formula says what its sentence says. Measuring that property, which we call \\emph{faithfulness}, is the bottleneck. Correct FOL is not unique: two systems can choose different predicate names, split a concept into different predicates, or write logically equivalent formulas, and all of these can be right.\n\nThe standard evaluation compares a candidate with a gold formula, by exact match, BLEU overlap or equivalence checked by a prover \\citep{Han2022,Yang2023,Thatikonda2025}. This comparison has two known failure modes. The gold itself is often wrong: a recent relabelling study reports incorrect formalizations in roughly 40\\% of the entries of the FOLIO validation and MALLS test splits \\citep{Brunello2026}. And a candidate can be faithful without being equivalent to the gold, because its vocabulary or granularity differs. Parse rate and structural checks avoid the gold but measure whether formulas are well formed and stable, not what they mean. Reference-free alternatives that read the text, such as LLM-as-a-judge \\citep{Zheng2023} and roundtrip verification \\citep{Amrollahi2026}, are the natural baselines, but they reward conventional vocabulary and they can share the blind spots of the systems they grade.\n\nA reference-free metric that does not read the text at all has one obvious source of evidence: the other systems. When several independent systems formalize the same sentence, their outputs can be compared with each other by a solver, without any gold and without trusting predicate names. Agreement of this kind is already used to \\emph{select} outputs in autoformalization \\citep{Li2024,Ryu2024}. Whether it \\emph{measures} faithfulness, how much it adds to baselines that read the text, and where it breaks has not been tested on real outputs against labels that do not share its machinery.\n\nWe test that question on outputs of nine current LLMs. We score a candidate by the share, weighted by system reliability, of the other systems' formulas that an SMT solver proves logically equivalent to it after a vocabulary alignment that never reads predicate names; we call this the \\emph{peer agreement score} and define it in Section~\\ref{sec:method}. We freeze its configuration on 700 development sentences and evaluate it on 450 fresh sentences from MALLS, FOLIO and ProverQA, under two independent label families: blinded adjudication by a calibrated panel of three LLMs, and solver equivalence to gold audited by the panel. The evidence supports a complement to a judge, not a replacement, and it is preliminary. Peer agreement is a strong standalone predictor and is exactly invariant to renaming, but its added value over baselines that read the text sits at the edge of statistical significance, it ties an existing latent-class agreement score, and it fails whenever most systems make the same mistake.\n\n\\paragraph{Contributions.}\n\\begin{itemize}\n  \\item A peer agreement score for NL$\\rightarrow$FOL faithfulness that ignores predicate names, weights systems by reliability and was frozen before evaluation (Section~\\ref{sec:method}). On 450 fresh sentences it reaches 0.827 AUROC against panel labels and 0.874 against audited solver labels, against 0.791 and 0.727 for a gemini-2.5-flash judge (Section~\\ref{sec:main}).\n  \\item An estimate of what it adds. Stacked on a base of judge, roundtrip and structural scores, it adds $+0.033$ AUROC on panel labels (95\\% CI [$-0.001$, 0.066]) and $+0.118$ on solver labels. It does not beat binary Dawid--Skene agreement (0.830), and its components for direction and error typing add nothing (Sections~\\ref{sec:increment} and~\\ref{sec:ablation}).\n  \\item A mapped failure boundary. The score is exactly invariant to predicate renaming, where the judge loses 0.151 AUROC on a vocabulary of random tokens (Section~\\ref{sec:invariance}). It falls to 0.419 AUROC on sentences whose majority meaning is wrong, and to 0.705 against the judge's 0.927 on long legal definitions (Sections~\\ref{sec:sharedbias} and~\\ref{sec:complexity}).\n  \\item A use where agreement is clearly useful: flagging wrong benchmark gold, at 0.837 to 0.859 AUROC and $+0.070$ over a judge run on the gold alone (Section~\\ref{sec:gold}).\n  \\item Negative results for three other reference-free families, a monotonicity signature, judgment worlds built by a solver and instance consequence NLI with a small model, none of which beats the judge on current systems (Section~\\ref{sec:otherfamilies}).\n\\end{itemize}\n\nFigure~\\ref{fig:headline} summarizes the finding. Section~\\ref{sec:related} places the work, Section~\\ref{sec:method} defines the score, Section~\\ref{sec:setup} gives the data, labels and protocol, Section~\\ref{sec:results} reports results, and Sections~\\ref{sec:discussion} to~\\ref{sec:conclusion} discuss them, state the limits and conclude.\n\n\\begin{figure}[!htbp]\n  \\centering\n  \\includegraphics[width=\\linewidth,height=0.85\\textheight,keepaspectratio]{figures/fig1_v0.pdf}\n  \\caption{Peer agreement on 450 fresh sentences formalized by nine LLMs. (a) AUROC with 95\\% intervals from a bootstrap clustered by sentence, under labels from a blinded LLM panel (256 items) and audited solver labels (3,720 rows; roundtrip NLI on 260 rows). Peer agreement is above the gemini-2.5-flash judge under both label families and ties binary Dawid--Skene agreement; parse rate and the structural consistency metrics are near chance. (b) AUROC under panel labels, split by whether the sentence's modal equivalence cluster is faithful. When most systems share an error, agreement falls below chance while the judge is unaffected.}\n  \\label{fig:headline}\n\\end{figure}\n\n%======================================================================\n\\section{Related Work}\n\\label{sec:related}\n\n\\paragraph{Evaluation against gold and label noise.} FOLIO \\citep{Han2022}, MALLS \\citep{Yang2023} and ProverQA \\citep{Qi2025} supply gold FOL for each sentence and are scored by equivalence or string overlap with the gold. A perturbation study of FOL closeness metrics shows that surface metrics such as BLEU react to text edits more than to operator edits \\citep{Thatikonda2025}. For text-to-SQL, test-suite accuracy compares denotations on distinguishing databases \\citep{Zhong2020}, and formal verification has exposed errors in that evaluation \\citep{Klopfenstein2025}. All of these assume a trustworthy gold. \\citet{Brunello2026} relabel FOLIO and MALLS and propose an LLM-assisted framework to direct human reviewers to suspect items; label-error detection with LLM ensembles has also been studied for general NLP benchmarks \\citep{Nahum2024}. We use gold only to build labels, audit it with an LLM panel, and use agreement to flag wrong gold, but we do not compare head to head with the relabelling framework.\n\n\\paragraph{Reference-free faithfulness.} LLM-as-a-judge \\citep{Zheng2023}, roundtrip verification \\citep{Amrollahi2026} and scoring of clause conformance \\citep{Liu2026} compare a formula, or its back-translation, with the text through a language model. FormalAlign trains an alignment scorer between informal and formal statements \\citep{Lu2024}, GenV trains a generative verifier of equivalence to a reference \\citep{Singh2026}, and certification that informal and formal statements are equivalent has been proposed for mathematics \\citep{Mohammad2026}. Entailment-preserving rates score FOL representations without a reference, but need entailment labels over several premises \\citep{Lee2025}. Roundtrip formalization, with equivalence checked by a solver, has been used to evaluate LLMs on truth maintenance without human labels \\citep{Karia2024}, and the metrics used for statement autoformalization have themselves been benchmarked against human judgments \\citep{Poiroux2025}. Faithfulness of autoformalization in legal reasoning has been examined separately \\citep{Wang2026}. Structural probes that need a gold formula, such as the polarity evaluation of SyGNS \\citep{Yanaka2021} compare monotonicity marks with a gold formula. These methods all read the text or a reference; our score reads neither, which makes it immune to vocabulary effects and blind to errors the systems share.\n\n\\paragraph{Agreement among outputs.} Self-consistency scores agreement within one model's samples \\citep{Wang2022}, and semantic entropy clusters sampled generations by bidirectional entailment to estimate uncertainty and detect hallucinations \\citep{Kuhn2023,Farquhar2024}. Symbolic-equivalence consistency clusters autoformalizations by solver equivalence and selects from the largest cluster \\citep{Li2024}; verification with a SAT solver is used to choose among compositional FOL translations \\citep{Ryu2024}; measures based on grammars quantify uncertainty over formal outputs \\citep{Ganguly2025}; LINC votes over prover answers \\citep{Olausson2023}. Distinguishing inputs judged by an oracle are used to select among programs \\citep{Fan2024}. These works use agreement within one model to estimate uncertainty, or agreement among outputs to choose one. We treat agreement across systems as a measurement, compare it with majority clustering in the style of \\citet{Li2024}, and report its failure regime.\n\n\\paragraph{Estimation without a gold standard.} Latent-class models estimate rater error rates without a gold standard \\citep{Dawid1979,Hui1980} and are known to be biased when raters' errors are conditionally dependent \\citep{Albert2004}. Benchmarking of LLM judgments without a gold standard has been proposed with a similar logic \\citep{Xu2024}. Our reliability weights come from a one-coin Dawid--Skene model, that is, one with a single accuracy parameter per rater, and our result on shared error is the failure under conditional dependence known in this literature, measured directly for NL$\\rightarrow$FOL.\n\n%======================================================================", "stderr": "", "interrupted": false, "isImage": false, "noOutputExpected": false}

OUT = Path(__file__).parent / "data.json"


def r3(x):
    return None if x is None else round(float(x), 3)


def ci(c):
    return [r3(c[0]), r3(c[1])] if c else None


# ---------- 1. leaderboard (tests.json) ----------
tests = json.loads((E3 / "tests.json").read_text())
METRICS = [
    ("DC", "Peer agreement (ours)", "agreement"),
    ("LC_ds_binary", "Binary Dawid–Skene agreement", "agreement"),
    ("LC_huiwalter", "Latent class, two populations (Hui–Walter)", "agreement"),
    ("LC_onecoin", "One-coin Dawid–Skene posterior", "agreement"),
    ("LC_maj", "Majority equivalence clustering", "agreement"),
    ("B1", "LLM judge (gemini-2.5-flash)", "reads text"),
    ("B3nliL", "Roundtrip NLI (local)", "reads text"),
    ("B3cosL", "Roundtrip cosine (local)", "reads text"),
    ("TJ_L", "Judgment worlds (local)", "reads text"),
    ("VC", "Vocabulary-conformity control", "control"),
    ("B7", "Structural consistency metrics", "structure"),
    ("B2", "Parse rate", "structure"),
]
board = []
for code, name, fam in METRICS:
    row = {"code": code, "name": name, "family": fam}
    for lab in ("panel", "solver"):
        a = tests["auroc"][f"{code}|{lab}"]
        row[lab] = {"auc": r3(a["auc"]), "ci": ci(a["ci95"]), "n": a["n"]}
    board.append(row)

t1 = tests["T1"]
increment = {
    lab: {
        "base": r3(t1[lab]["auc_base"]), "plus": r3(t1[lab]["auc_base_plus"]),
        "delta": r3(t1[lab]["point"]), "ci": ci(t1[lab]["ci95"]), "n": t1[lab]["n"],
        "placebo": r3(t1[lab]["placebo"]["point"]), "placebo_ci": ci(t1[lab]["placebo"]["ci95"]),
    }
    for lab in ("panel", "solver")
}
t2 = tests["T2"]["panel"]
increment["vs_panel"] = {k: {"delta": r3(t2[k]["point"]), "ci": ci(t2[k]["ci95"])} for k in ("LC_maj", "LC_ds_binary", "VC")}

# ---------- 2. shared error ----------
m3 = json.loads((E4 / "m3_boundary.json").read_text())
dose = {}
for order in ("random", "faithful_first"):
    dose[order] = []
    for k in (0, 2, 4, 6, 8):
        p = m3["a_dose"][order][f"k={k}"]["pooled"]["det_DC_L2"]
        dose[order].append({"k": k, "v": r3(p["mean"]), "ci": ci(p["ci"]), "n": p["n"]})
bins = []
for b, v in m3["c_real"]["bins"].items():
    bins.append({"bin": b, "v": r3(v["DC"]["mean"]), "ci": ci(v["DC"]["ci"]), "n_pairs": v["n_pairs"], "n_sent": v["n_sentences"]})
an = json.loads((E3 / "analysis.json").read_text())
sb = an["shared_bias"]["panel"]
mode_split = {
    grp: {m: {"auc": r3(sb[grp][m]["auc"]), "ci": ci(sb[grp][m]["ci95"]), "n": sb[grp][m]["n"], "n_pos": sb[grp][m]["n_pos"]}
          for m in ("DC", "LC_maj", "B1")}
    for grp in ("mode_right", "mode_wrong")
}

# ---------- 3. vocabulary invariance ----------
m1 = json.loads((E4 / "m1_confound.json").read_text())
ARMS = [("conf", "Conventional names"), ("tok", "Random tokens"), ("syn", "WordNet synonyms"), ("crossed", "Crossed: faithful in tokens, mutants conventional")]
INV_M = [("DC_L2w", "Peer agreement, no granularity defs (ours)"), ("LC_maj_star", "Majority equivalence clustering"),
         ("B1", "LLM judge (gemini-2.5-flash)"), ("VC", "Vocabulary-conformity control")]
invariance = {"metrics": [n for _, n in INV_M], "arms": []}
for key, label in ARMS:
    src = m1["crossed"] if key == "crossed" else m1["arms"][key]
    invariance["arms"].append({"key": key, "label": label,
                               "vals": [{"auc": r3(src[c]["auroc"]), "ci": ci(src[c]["ci"])} for c, _ in INV_M],
                               "n_F": src["DC_L2w"]["n_F"], "n_M": src["DC_L2w"]["n_M"]})

# ---------- 4. complexity ----------
ae = json.loads((E3 / "analysis_extra.json").read_text())
fig5 = json.loads(Path("figures/fig5_spec.json").read_text())
complexity = {}
for g in fig5["panel_a"]["groups"]:
    complexity[g["header"]] = [{"label": r["label"], "n": r["n"], "n_pos": r["n_faithful"],
                                "DC": {"auc": r3(r["peer_agreement"]["auroc"]), "ci": ci(r["peer_agreement"]["ci95"])},
                                "B1": {"auc": r3(r["llm_judge"]["auroc"]), "ci": ci(r["llm_judge"]["ci95"])}} for r in g["rows"]]
x1 = json.loads((E5 / "tests.json").read_text())["X1"]
x3 = json.loads((E5 / "tests.json").read_text())["X3"]["per_bin"]
legal_rows = [{"label": "All legal items", "n": x1["n"], "n_pos": x1["n_pos"],
               "DC": {"auc": r3(x1["baselines"]["DC"]["auroc_w"]), "ci": ci(x1["baselines"]["DC"]["ci95"])},
               "B1": {"auc": r3(x1["baselines"]["B1"]["auroc_w"]), "ci": ci(x1["baselines"]["B1"]["ci95"])}}]
for key, lab in (("B0", "0–1 markers"), ("B1", "2–3 markers"), ("B2", "≥4 markers")):
    b = x3[key]
    legal_rows.append({"label": lab, "n": b["DC"]["n"], "n_pos": b["DC"]["n_pos"],
                       "DC": {"auc": r3(b["DC"]["auroc_w"]), "ci": ci(b["DC"]["ci95"])},
                       "B1": {"auc": r3(b["B1"]["auroc_w"]), "ci": ci(b["B1"]["ci95"])}})
complexity["Legal definitions (exception markers)"] = legal_rows

m7 = json.loads((E4 / "m7_goldflag.json").read_text())
goldflag = {"n": m7["n_golds"], "wrong_rate": r3(m7["wrong_gold_rate"]),
            "DC": {"auc": r3(m7["DC_gold_auroc_vs_L0"]["auroc"]), "ci": ci(m7["DC_gold_auroc_vs_L0"]["ci"])},
            "judge_oof": r3(m7["stack_B1_plus_DC"]["auroc_judge_oof"]), "judge_plus": r3(m7["stack_B1_plus_DC"]["auroc_judge_plus_DC_oof"]),
            "delta": r3(m7["stack_B1_plus_DC"]["delta"]), "delta_ci": ci(m7["stack_B1_plus_DC"]["ci"]),
            "per_corpus": {c: {"n": v["n"], "wrong": r3(v["wrong_rate"]), "auc": r3(v["DC_auroc"])} for c, v in m7["per_corpus"].items()}}

# ---------- 6. item explorer (greedy candidates, 450 sentences x 9 systems) ----------
sc = defaultdict(dict)
with open(E3 / "scores.jsonl") as f:
    for line in f:
        d = json.loads(line)
        if d["metric"] in ("DC", "B1", "LC_maj"):
            sc[d["item_id"]][d["metric"]] = d
sents = {}
with open(E3 / "fresh_set.jsonl") as f:
    for line in f:
        r = json.loads(line)
        if r["fold"] != "fresh_greedy":
            continue
        s = sents.setdefault(r["sid"], {"sid": r["sid"], "t": r["sentence"], "c": r["corpus"], "tok": r["n_tokens"],
                                        "g": r["gold_fol_audited"], "go": r["gold_fol_original"], "gs": r["gold_source"], "cands": []})
        m = sc.get(r["item_id"], {})
        dc = m.get("DC")
        ex = dc["extra"] if dc else {}
        panel = None
        if r["label_source"] == "panel3" and r["L3_majority"] is not None:
            panel = 1 if r["L3_majority"] else 0
        s["cands"].append({
            "sys": r["system"], "f": r["cand"], "p": int(bool(r["parse_ok"])),
            "sol": {"faithful": 1, "unfaithful": 0}.get(r["output"]),
            "pan": panel, "err": r["L3_primary_error"] if panel == 0 else None,
            "dc": r3(dc["score"]) if dc and dc["covered"] else None,
            "b1": r3(m["B1"]["score"]) if "B1" in m and m["B1"]["covered"] else None,
            "lc": r3(m["LC_maj"]["score"]) if "LC_maj" in m and m["LC_maj"]["covered"] else None,
            "mode": int(bool(ex.get("in_mode"))) if ex else None,
            "rel": ex.get("relations") or {},
        })
        s["nc"] = ex.get("n_clusters", s.get("nc"))
        s["ms"] = r3(ex.get("mode_weight_share")) if ex.get("mode_weight_share") is not None else s.get("ms")
items = sorted(sents.values(), key=lambda s: (s["c"], s["sid"]))
for s in items:
    s["cands"].sort(key=lambda c: c["sys"])

data = {"board": board, "labels": tests["label_counts"], "increment": increment, "dose": dose, "bins": bins,
        "slope": [r3(m3["c_real"]["logistic_slope_det_on_wrong_conc"])] + ci(m3["c_real"]["slope_ci"]),
        "mode_split": mode_split, "invariance": invariance, "complexity": complexity, "goldflag": goldflag, "items": items}
OUT.write_text(json.dumps(data, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":")))
print("items", len(items), "cands", sum(len(s["cands"]) for s in items), "bytes", OUT.stat().st_size)
print("panel-labelled", sum(c["pan"] is not None for s in items for c in s["cands"]))
print(json.dumps(bins), json.dumps(increment)[:400])

<div class="wrap">
<header>
  <p class="kicker">Interactive companion · <a href="index.html">back to the paper page</a></p>
  <h1>Does agreement among nine LLMs tell you whether a logic formula matches its sentence?</h1>
  <p>Each sentence is translated into first-order logic by nine LLMs. A candidate's <strong>peer agreement score</strong> is the reliability-weighted share of the other systems' formulas that an SMT solver proves equivalent to it, after a vocabulary alignment that never reads predicate names. Weights come from a one-coin Dawid–Skene model fitted without labels, and the configuration was frozen on 700 development sentences before the 450 fresh sentences shown here were scored.</p>
  <p>Every chart below is drawn from the run's result files. Use the controls to test each claim yourself.</p>
  <nav class="toc" aria-label="Sections">
    <a href="#board">1 · Which metric predicts faithfulness</a>
    <a href="#adds">2 · What it adds</a>
    <a href="#shared">3 · Shared errors</a>
    <a href="#vocab">4 · Renaming predicates</a>
    <a href="#complex">5 · Complexity</a>
    <a href="#gold">6 · Wrong gold</a>
    <a href="#explore">7 · Browse the formulas</a>
  </nav>
</header>

<section id="board">
  <h2>1 · Which metric predicts faithfulness?</h2>
  <p class="q">Rank every reference-free metric by AUROC (faithful vs. unfaithful), under either label family.</p>
  <div class="controls">
    <span>Labels:</span>
    <div class="seg" role="group" aria-label="Label family" id="boardLab">
      <button aria-pressed="true" data-v="panel">Blinded LLM panel (256 items)</button>
      <button aria-pressed="false" data-v="solver">Audited solver (3,720 rows)</button>
    </div>
    <label class="chk"><input type="checkbox" id="boardSort" checked> Sort by AUROC</label>
  </div>
  <div class="legend">
    <span style="--sw:var(--c-ours)">Peer agreement (ours)</span>
    <span style="--sw:var(--c-agree)">Other agreement estimators</span>
    <span style="--sw:var(--c-text)">Reads the text</span>
    <span style="--sw:var(--c-ctrl)">Control</span>
    <span style="--sw:var(--c-struct)">Structure only</span>
  </div>
  <div class="card"><svg id="boardSvg" role="img" aria-label="AUROC by metric with 95% intervals"></svg></div>
  <p class="note" id="boardNote"></p>
</section>

<section id="adds">
  <h2>2 · What does it add to baselines that read the text?</h2>
  <p class="q">Stack the score on a base of judge, roundtrip and structural scores, then measure the cross-fitted AUROC gain.</p>
  <div class="grid2" id="addCards"></div>
  <div class="card" style="margin-top:1rem">
    <h3>Peer agreement minus its neighbours (panel labels, ΔAUROC in the same stack)</h3>
    <svg id="vsSvg" role="img" aria-label="Increment over neighbouring agreement metrics"></svg>
  </div>
  <p class="note">A placebo random feature added the same way is shown for scale. On panel labels the gain's 95% interval touches zero, and the score does not beat binary Dawid–Skene agreement.</p>
</section>

<section id="shared">
  <h2>3 · When do shared errors break agreement?</h2>
  <p class="q">Replace k of the 8 peers with copies of a wrong formula and see whether the faithful candidate still outscores the error.</p>
  <div class="controls">
    <label for="doseK">Peers replaced by the error, k = <strong id="doseKv">0</strong> of 8</label>
    <input type="range" id="doseK" min="0" max="8" step="2" value="0">
    <div class="seg" role="group" aria-label="Replacement order" id="doseOrder">
      <button aria-pressed="true" data-v="random">In random order</button>
      <button aria-pressed="false" data-v="faithful_first">Faithful peers first</button>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="grid2">
    <div class="card">
      <div class="stat" id="doseStat"></div>
      <p class="kv" id="doseKv2"></p>
      <svg id="doseSvg" role="img" aria-label="Detection rate against k"></svg>
    </div>
    <div class="card">
      <h3>Real data: detection by the peer weight on wrong meanings</h3>
      <svg id="binSvg" role="img" aria-label="Within-sentence concordance by wrong-cluster share"></svg>
      <p class="kv" id="slopeKv"></p>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="card" style="margin-top:1rem">
    <h3>Fresh set, split by whether the sentence's largest equivalence cluster is faithful (panel labels)</h3>
    <svg id="modeSvg" role="img" aria-label="AUROC split by modal cluster faithfulness"></svg>
  </div>
  <p class="note">Controlled test on 200 development sentences, 560 items per k, with alignment levels L1 and L2 only. Detection is the probability that the faithful formula scores above the mutant. On the fresh set, agreement drops below chance when the majority is wrong, while the judge is unaffected.</p>
</section>

<section id="vocab">
  <h2>4 · Does renaming the predicates fool it?</h2>
  <p class="q">Rewrite 223 faithful formulas and 739 solver-verified mutants in different vocabularies and see which scores move.</p>
  <div class="controls">
    <span>Vocabulary:</span>
    <div class="seg" role="group" aria-label="Vocabulary arm" id="vocArm"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="card"><svg id="vocSvg" role="img" aria-label="AUROC per metric under the chosen vocabulary"></svg></div>
  <p class="note" id="vocNote"></p>
</section>

<section id="complex">
  <h2>5 · How does it hold up as sentences get more complex?</h2>
  <p class="q">Compare peer agreement with the LLM judge, one complexity stratum at a time.</p>
  <div class="controls">
    <label for="cxFacet">Split by</label>
    <select id="cxFacet"></select>
  </div>
  <div class="legend"><span style="--sw:var(--c-ours)">Peer agreement (ours)</span><span style="--sw:var(--c-text)">LLM judge (gemini-2.5-flash)</span></div>
  <div class="card"><svg id="cxSvg" role="img" aria-label="AUROC by complexity stratum"></svg></div>
  <p class="note" id="cxNote"></p>
</section>

<section id="gold">
  <h2>6 · Can agreement flag wrong benchmark gold?</h2>
  <p class="q">Score each benchmark gold formula against the nine systems' outputs, then check whether low agreement marks gold the panel audit rejected.</p>
  <div class="grid2" id="goldCards"></div>
</section>

<section id="explore">
  <h2>7 · Browse the 4,050 formalizations</h2>
  <p class="q">Pick a sentence and compare its nine formulas, their scores and both labels.</p>
  <div class="controls">
    <label for="exCorpus">Corpus</label>
    <select id="exCorpus"><option value="">All</option><option value="folio">FOLIO</option><option value="malls">MALLS</option><option value="proverqa">ProverQA</option></select>
    <label for="exFilter">Show</label>
    <select id="exFilter">
      <option value="">All sentences</option>
      <option value="panel">With panel labels</option>
      <option value="modewrong">Panel says a modal-cluster formula is unfaithful</option>
      <option value="disagree">Agreement and judge disagree sharply</option>
      <option value="goldfix">Audit replaced the benchmark gold</option>
    </select>
    <input type="search" id="exSearch" placeholder="Search sentence text" aria-label="Search sentence text">
  </div>
  <div class="explorer-nav">
    <button class="btn" id="exPrev" aria-label="Previous sentence">← Prev</button>
    <button class="btn" id="exNext" aria-label="Next sentence">Next →</button>
    <button class="btn" id="exRand">Random</button>
    <span class="count" id="exCount" aria-live="polite"></span>
  </div>
  <div class="card" id="exCard"></div>
  <p class="note">Peer agreement lies in [0, 1] (blank when fewer than two peers are comparable). Judge is the gemini-2.5-flash score. <em>Modal</em> marks membership of the sentence's heaviest equivalence cluster. Solver label: equivalence to the audited gold. Panel label: blinded three-LLM majority, available for 256 sampled candidates. The relation counts give the solver's verdict against each peer.</p>
</section>

<footer>
  <p>Data provenance. Everything on this page was extracted from the run's experiment outputs and embedded in this file:</p>
  <ul>
    <li>Sections 1–2 and 7: <code>gen_art_experiment_3/results/tests.json</code> (auroc, T1, T2), <code>fresh_set.jsonl</code> (greedy candidates, labels, gold), <code>scores.jsonl</code> (DC, B1, LC_maj scores)</li>
    <li>Section 3: <code>gen_art_experiment_4/results/m3_boundary.json</code> (a_dose pooled det_DC_L2, c_real bins) and <code>gen_art_experiment_3/results/analysis.json</code> (shared_bias.panel)</li>
    <li>Section 4: <code>gen_art_experiment_4/results/m1_confound.json</code> (arms conf/tok/syn, crossed)</li>
    <li>Section 5: <code>gen_art_experiment_3/results/analysis_extra.json</code> via <code>figures/fig5_spec.json</code>; legal set from <code>gen_art_experiment_5/results/tests.json</code> (X1, X3)</li>
    <li>Section 6: <code>gen_art_experiment_4/results/m7_goldflag.json</code></li>
  </ul>
  <p>Paths are relative to <code>run_ujABDGgoK_5Q/3_invention_loop/iter_2/gen_art/</code>. Intervals are 95% bootstrap intervals clustered by sentence.</p>
</footer>
</div>
<div class="tip" id="tip" role="tooltip"></div>
<script id="data" type="application/json">/*DATA*/</script>
<script>
(function () {
"use strict";
var D = JSON.parse(document.getElementById("data").textContent);
var NS = "http://www.w3.org/2000/svg";
var tip = document.getElementById("tip");
function f3(x) { return x == null ? "–" : x.toFixed(3); }
function sgn(x) { return (x >= 0 ? "+" : "−") + Math.abs(x).toFixed(3); }
function ciS(c) { return c ? "[" + f3(c[0]) + ", " + f3(c[1]) + "]" : ""; }
function el(tag, attrs, parent, text) {
  var e = document.createElementNS(NS, tag);
  for (var k in attrs) e.setAttribute(k, attrs[k]);
  if (text != null) e.textContent = text;
  if (parent) parent.appendChild(e);
  return e;
}
function esc(s) { return String(s).replace(/[&<>"]/g, function (c) { return { "&": "&amp;", "<": "&lt;", ">": "&gt;", '"': "&quot;" }[c]; }); }
function hoverable(node, html) {
  node.addEventListener("mousemove", function (ev) {
    tip.innerHTML = html; tip.style.opacity = 1;
    var x = Math.min(ev.clientX + 12, window.innerWidth - tip.offsetWidth - 8);
    tip.style.left = x + "px"; tip.style.top = (ev.clientY + 14) + "px";
  });
  node.addEventListener("mouseleave", function () { tip.style.opacity = 0; });
}
function segment(id, onChange) {
  var g = document.getElementById(id);
  g.addEventListener("click", function (ev) {
    var b = ev.target.closest("button"); if (!b) return;
    g.querySelectorAll("button").forEach(function (x) { x.setAttribute("aria-pressed", x === b ? "true" : "false"); });
    onChange(b.dataset.v);
  });
}
function clear(svg) { while (svg.firstChild) svg.removeChild(svg.firstChild); }
function width(svg) { return Math.max(300, svg.parentNode.clientWidth - 32); }
var FAM = { agreement: "var(--c-agree)", "reads text": "var(--c-text)", control: "var(--c-ctrl)", structure: "var(--c-struct)" };

/* Horizontal dot-with-interval chart. rows: [{label, auc, ci, color, bold, extra}] */
function hDots(svg, rows, opt) {
  clear(svg);
  var W = width(svg), narrow = W < 560;
  var labW = narrow ? Math.min(150, W * 0.42) : 260, rowH = narrow ? 34 : 28, top = 8, bottom = 34;
  var x0 = labW + 8, x1 = W - 44, lo = opt.lo, hi = opt.hi;
  var H = top + rows.length * rowH + bottom;
  svg.setAttribute("viewBox", "0 0 " + W + " " + H);
  function X(v) { return x0 + (Math.max(lo, Math.min(hi, v)) - lo) / (hi - lo) * (x1 - x0); }
  var gg = el("g", { class: "grid" }, svg);
  for (var t = Math.ceil(lo * 10) / 10; t <= hi + 1e-9; t += 0.1) {
    el("line", { x1: X(t), x2: X(t), y1: top, y2: H - bottom + 4 }, gg);
    el("text", { x: X(t), y: H - bottom + 18, "text-anchor": "middle", "font-size": 11 }, svg, t.toFixed(1));
  }
  if (opt.ref != null) {
    el("line", { x1: X(opt.ref), x2: X(opt.ref), y1: top, y2: H - bottom + 4, stroke: "var(--ink-3)", "stroke-dasharray": "4 3" }, svg);
    el("text", { x: X(opt.ref) + 4, y: top + 10, "font-size": 10.5 }, svg, opt.refLabel || "chance");
  }
  el("text", { x: (x0 + x1) / 2, y: H - 3, "text-anchor": "middle", "font-size": 11.5 }, svg, opt.xlabel || "AUROC");
  rows.forEach(function (r, i) {
    var y = top + i * rowH + rowH / 2;
    var g = el("g", {}, svg);
    var lt = el("text", { x: labW, y: y + 4, "text-anchor": "end", "font-size": narrow ? 11 : 12.5, "font-weight": r.bold ? 650 : 400 }, g);
    var lab = r.label, maxc = narrow ? 22 : 40;
    lt.textContent = lab.length > maxc ? lab.slice(0, maxc - 1) + "…" : lab;
    if (r.auc == null) { el("text", { x: x0 + 4, y: y + 4, "font-size": 11 }, g, "not measured"); return; }
    el("rect", { x: 0, y: y - rowH / 2, width: W, height: rowH, fill: "transparent" }, g);
    if (r.ci) el("line", { x1: X(r.ci[0]), x2: X(r.ci[1]), y1: y, y2: y, stroke: r.color, "stroke-width": 2.5, "stroke-linecap": "round", opacity: 0.55 }, g);
    el("circle", { cx: X(r.auc), cy: y, r: r.bold ? 6 : 5, fill: r.color, stroke: "var(--surface)", "stroke-width": 1.5 }, g);
    el("text", { x: Math.min(X(r.ci ? r.ci[1] : r.auc) + 8, W - 40), y: y + 4, "font-size": 11.5, "font-weight": r.bold ? 650 : 400 }, g, f3(r.auc));
    hoverable(g, "<strong>" + esc(r.label) + "</strong><br>" + (opt.valName || "AUROC") + " " + f3(r.auc) + (r.ci ? " " + ciS(r.ci) : "") + (r.extra ? "<br>" + r.extra : ""));
  });
}

/* ---------- 1. leaderboard ---------- */
var boardLab = "panel";
function drawBoard() {
  var rows = D.board.map(function (m) {
    var v = m[boardLab];
    return { label: m.name, auc: v.auc, ci: v.ci, color: m.code === "DC" ? "var(--c-ours)" : FAM[m.family], bold: m.code === "DC", extra: "n = " + v.n.toLocaleString() + " · " + m.family };
  });
  if (document.getElementById("boardSort").checked) rows.sort(function (a, b) { return b.auc - a.auc; });
  hDots(document.getElementById("boardSvg"), rows, { lo: 0.4, hi: 1.0, ref: 0.5, xlabel: "AUROC (faithful vs. unfaithful)" });
  var dc = D.board[0][boardLab], j = D.board.filter(function (m) { return m.code === "B1"; })[0][boardLab];
  var lc = D.labels[boardLab];
  document.getElementById("boardNote").textContent = boardLab === "panel"
    ? "Panel labels: majority vote of three blinded LLMs on 256 sampled candidates (" + lc["1"] + " faithful, " + lc["0"] + " unfaithful). Peer agreement " + f3(dc.auc) + " vs. judge " + f3(j.auc) + ". Roundtrip and judgment-worlds metrics were run on the panel items only."
    : "Solver labels: equivalence to benchmark gold after a panel audit, on 3,720 greedy candidates (" + lc["1"].toLocaleString() + " faithful, " + lc["0"].toLocaleString() + " unfaithful). Peer agreement " + f3(dc.auc) + " vs. judge " + f3(j.auc) + ". Local roundtrip and judgment worlds have only 260 solver-labelled rows, so their intervals are wide.";
}
segment("boardLab", function (v) { boardLab = v; drawBoard(); });
document.getElementById("boardSort").addEventListener("change", drawBoard);

/* ---------- 2. increment ---------- */
(function () {
  var host = document.getElementById("addCards"), I = D.increment;
  [["panel", "Panel labels"], ["solver", "Solver labels (panel items with a solver label)"]].forEach(function (p) {
    var v = I[p[0]], crosses = v.ci[0] <= 0;
    var d = document.createElement("div"); d.className = "card";
    d.innerHTML = "<h3>" + p[1] + "</h3><div class='stat'>" + sgn(v.delta) + " <small>AUROC</small></div>" +
      "<p class='kv'>95% CI " + ciS(v.ci) + (crosses ? ": touches zero" : ": excludes zero") + "</p>" +
      "<p class='kv'>Base " + f3(v.base) + " → base + peer agreement " + f3(v.plus) + " (n = " + v.n + ")</p>" +
      "<p class='kv'>Placebo random feature: " + sgn(v.placebo) + " " + ciS(v.placebo_ci) + "</p>";
    host.appendChild(d);
  });
  var names = { LC_maj: "vs. majority equivalence clustering", LC_ds_binary: "vs. binary Dawid–Skene", VC: "vs. vocabulary-conformity control" };
  var rows = Object.keys(I.vs_panel).map(function (k) { var v = I.vs_panel[k]; return { label: names[k], auc: v.delta, ci: v.ci, color: "var(--c-ours)" }; });
  rows.push({ label: "placebo random feature", auc: I.panel.placebo, ci: I.panel.placebo_ci, color: "var(--c-struct)" });
  function draw() { hDots(document.getElementById("vsSvg"), rows, { lo: -0.1, hi: 0.3, ref: 0, refLabel: "no gain", xlabel: "ΔAUROC", valName: "Δ" }); }
  draw(); window.addEventListener("resize", draw);
})();

/* ---------- 3. shared errors ---------- */
var doseOrder = "random";
function drawDose() {
  var k = +document.getElementById("doseK").value;
  document.getElementById("doseKv").textContent = k;
  var S = D.dose[doseOrder], pt = S.filter(function (p) { return p.k === k; })[0];
  document.getElementById("doseStat").innerHTML = f3(pt.v) + " <small>detection</small>";
  document.getElementById("doseKv2").textContent = "95% CI " + ciS(pt.ci) + " · " + pt.n + " items · " + (pt.v > 0.5 ? "above" : pt.v === 0.5 ? "at" : "below") + " chance";
  var svg = document.getElementById("doseSvg"); clear(svg);
  var W = width(svg), H = 230, l = 44, r = 14, t = 14, b = 40;
  svg.setAttribute("viewBox", "0 0 " + W + " " + H);
  function X(v) { return l + v / 8 * (W - l - r); } function Y(v) { return t + (1 - v) * (H - t - b); }
  [0, .25, .5, .75, 1].forEach(function (v) {
    el("line", { x1: l, x2: W - r, y1: Y(v), y2: Y(v), stroke: v === .5 ? "var(--ink-3)" : "var(--rule)", "stroke-dasharray": v === .5 ? "4 3" : "" }, svg);
    el("text", { x: l - 6, y: Y(v) + 4, "text-anchor": "end", "font-size": 11 }, svg, v.toFixed(2));
  });
  [0, 2, 4, 6, 8].forEach(function (kk) { el("text", { x: X(kk), y: H - b + 16, "text-anchor": "middle", "font-size": 11 }, svg, kk); });
  el("text", { x: (l + W - r) / 2, y: H - 4, "text-anchor": "middle", "font-size": 11.5 }, svg, "k = peers replaced by copies of the error");
  ["faithful_first", "random"].forEach(function (o) {
    var s = D.dose[o], on = o === doseOrder, col = on ? "var(--c-ours)" : "var(--c-struct)";
    var band = s.map(function (p) { return X(p.k) + "," + Y(p.ci[1]); }).concat(s.slice().reverse().map(function (p) { return X(p.k) + "," + Y(p.ci[0]); }));
    if (on) el("polygon", { points: band.join(" "), fill: "var(--c-ours)", opacity: 0.12 }, svg);
    el("polyline", { points: s.map(function (p) { return X(p.k) + "," + Y(p.v); }).join(" "), fill: "none", stroke: col, "stroke-width": on ? 2.5 : 1.5 }, svg);
    s.forEach(function (p) { el("circle", { cx: X(p.k), cy: Y(p.v), r: on ? 3.5 : 2.5, fill: col }, svg); });
  });
  el("circle", { cx: X(k), cy: Y(pt.v), r: 7.5, fill: "none", stroke: "var(--ink)", "stroke-width": 2 }, svg);
}
document.getElementById("doseK").addEventListener("input", drawDose);
segment("doseOrder", function (v) { doseOrder = v; drawDose(); });

function drawBins() {
  var svg = document.getElementById("binSvg"); clear(svg);
  var W = width(svg), H = 230, l = 44, r = 10, t = 14, b = 46, n = D.bins.length;
  svg.setAttribute("viewBox", "0 0 " + W + " " + H);
  function Y(v) { return t + (1 - v) * (H - t - b); }
  [0, .25, .5, .75, 1].forEach(function (v) {
    el("line", { x1: l, x2: W - r, y1: Y(v), y2: Y(v), stroke: v === .5 ? "var(--ink-3)" : "var(--rule)", "stroke-dasharray": v === .5 ? "4 3" : "" }, svg);
    el("text", { x: l - 6, y: Y(v) + 4, "text-anchor": "end", "font-size": 11 }, svg, v.toFixed(2));
  });
  var bw = (W - l - r) / n;
  D.bins.forEach(function (bn, i) {
    var x = l + i * bw + bw * 0.18, w = bw * 0.64, wrong = i >= 2;
    var g = el("g", {}, svg);
    el("rect", { x: x, y: Y(bn.v), width: w, height: Y(0) - Y(bn.v), fill: wrong ? "var(--c-ctrl)" : "var(--c-ours)", rx: 2 }, g);
    el("line", { x1: x + w / 2, x2: x + w / 2, y1: Y(bn.ci[0]), y2: Y(bn.ci[1]), stroke: "var(--ink)", "stroke-width": 1.5 }, g);
    el("text", { x: x + w / 2, y: Y(bn.ci[1]) - 5, "text-anchor": "middle", "font-size": 11 }, g, f3(bn.v));
    el("text", { x: x + w / 2, y: H - b + 16, "text-anchor": "middle", "font-size": 11 }, svg, bn.bin.replace("[0.75,1.0)", "≥0.75").replace(",", ", "));
    hoverable(g, "Wrong-meaning share " + esc(bn.bin) + "<br>concordance " + f3(bn.v) + " " + ciS(bn.ci) + "<br>" + bn.n_pairs.toLocaleString() + " pairs, " + bn.n_sent + " sentences");
  });
  el("text", { x: (l + W - r) / 2, y: H - 6, "text-anchor": "middle", "font-size": 11.5 }, svg, "peer-weight share of wrong-meaning clusters");
  document.getElementById("slopeKv").textContent = "Logistic slope of detection on the wrong share: " + D.slope[0].toFixed(2) + " [" + D.slope[1].toFixed(2) + ", " + D.slope[2].toFixed(2) + "], on 6,772 development pairs.";
}
function drawMode() {
  var M = D.mode_split, names = { DC: "Peer agreement (ours)", LC_maj: "Majority equivalence clustering", B1: "LLM judge (gemini-2.5-flash)" }, rows = [];
  [["mode_right", "Modal cluster faithful"], ["mode_wrong", "Modal cluster unfaithful"]].forEach(function (g) {
    ["DC", "LC_maj", "B1"].forEach(function (m) {
      var v = M[g[0]][m];
      rows.push({ label: g[1].replace("Modal cluster ", "") + " · " + names[m], auc: v.auc, ci: v.ci, bold: m === "DC",
        color: m === "DC" ? "var(--c-ours)" : m === "B1" ? "var(--c-text)" : "var(--c-agree)", extra: g[1] + ": n = " + v.n + ", " + v.n_pos + " faithful" });
    });
  });
  hDots(document.getElementById("modeSvg"), rows, { lo: 0.2, hi: 1.0, ref: 0.5, xlabel: "AUROC (panel labels)" });
}

/* ---------- 4. vocabulary ---------- */
var vocArm = 0;
(function () {
  var g = document.getElementById("vocArm");
  D.invariance.arms.forEach(function (a, i) {
    var b = document.createElement("button"); b.dataset.v = i; b.textContent = a.key === "crossed" ? "Crossed" : a.label;
    b.setAttribute("aria-pressed", i === 0 ? "true" : "false"); g.appendChild(b);
  });
  segment("vocArm", function (v) { vocArm = +v; drawVoc(); });
})();
function drawVoc() {
  var A = D.invariance.arms[vocArm], base = D.invariance.arms[0];
  var cols = ["var(--c-ours)", "var(--c-agree)", "var(--c-text)", "var(--c-ctrl)"];
  var rows = D.invariance.metrics.map(function (m, i) {
    var d = A.vals[i].auc - base.vals[i].auc;
    return { label: m, auc: A.vals[i].auc, ci: A.vals[i].ci, color: cols[i], bold: i === 0, extra: vocArm ? "Change vs. conventional names: " + sgn(d) : "" };
  });
  hDots(document.getElementById("vocSvg"), rows, { lo: 0.1, hi: 1.0, ref: 0.5, xlabel: "AUROC (faithful vs. mutant)" });
  var j = A.vals[2].auc - base.vals[2].auc;
  document.getElementById("vocNote").textContent = A.label + ": " + A.n_F + " faithful formulas and " + A.n_M + " mutants. " +
    (vocArm === 0 ? "Pick another vocabulary to see which scores move." :
      "Peer agreement changes by " + sgn(A.vals[0].auc - base.vals[0].auc) + " and the judge by " + sgn(j) + " relative to conventional names." +
      (A.key === "crossed" ? " The vocabulary-conformity control falls far below chance, because it rewards conventional names rather than meaning." : ""));
}

/* ---------- 5. complexity ---------- */
(function () {
  var s = document.getElementById("cxFacet");
  Object.keys(D.complexity).forEach(function (k) { var o = document.createElement("option"); o.value = k; o.textContent = k === "Tokens" ? "Sentence length (tokens)" : k.indexOf("Legal") === 0 ? k : "Number of " + k.toLowerCase().replace("nesting depth", "nesting levels"); s.appendChild(o); });
  s.addEventListener("change", drawCx);
})();
function drawCx() {
  var k = document.getElementById("cxFacet").value, R = D.complexity[k], rows = [];
  R.forEach(function (r) {
    rows.push({ label: r.label + " · peer agreement", auc: r.DC.auc, ci: r.DC.ci, color: "var(--c-ours)", bold: true, extra: "n = " + r.n + ", " + r.n_pos + " faithful" });
    rows.push({ label: r.label + " · LLM judge", auc: r.B1.auc, ci: r.B1.ci, color: "var(--c-text)", extra: "n = " + r.n + ", " + r.n_pos + " faithful" });
  });
  hDots(document.getElementById("cxSvg"), rows, { lo: 0.2, hi: 1.0, ref: 0.5, xlabel: "AUROC (panel labels)" });
  var legal = k.indexOf("Legal") === 0;
  var wins = R.filter(function (r) { return r.DC.auc > r.B1.auc; }).length;
  document.getElementById("cxNote").textContent = (legal
    ? "Legal set: 158 definitions from EU and US law, 655 panel-labelled candidates judged from the sentence alone (weighted AUROC). The panel's labels are weakest here (Fleiss κ = 0.17 at ≥4 markers), and the higher-marker bins have few faithful items. "
    : "Fresh set, 256 panel items. ") + "Peer agreement leads the judge in " + wins + " of " + R.length + " rows.";
}

/* ---------- 6. wrong gold ---------- */
(function () {
  var G = D.goldflag, host = document.getElementById("goldCards");
  var a = document.createElement("div"); a.className = "card";
  a.innerHTML = "<h3>Agreement as a wrong-gold detector</h3><div class='stat'>" + f3(G.DC.auc) + " <small>AUROC</small></div>" +
    "<p class='kv'>95% CI " + ciS(G.DC.ci) + " on " + G.n + " development gold formulas, of which " + Math.round(G.wrong_rate * 100) + "% were judged wrong by the audit.</p>" +
    "<p class='kv'>Judge on the gold alone " + f3(G.judge_oof) + " → judge + agreement " + f3(G.judge_plus) + " (" + sgn(G.delta) + ", CI " + ciS(G.delta_ci) + ")</p>";
  var b = document.createElement("div"); b.className = "card";

  h += "<div class='tablewrap'><table><thead><tr><th>System</th><th>Formula</th><th class='num'>Peer agreement</th><th class='num'>Judge</th><th>Solver label</th><th>Panel label</th></tr></thead><tbody>";

  });

document.getElementById("exRand").addEventListener("click", function () { if (list.length) { pos = Math.floor(Math.random() * list.length); drawEx(); } });
